newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar ends steady in range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar ends steady in range-bound trade.

text.p: Indian sugar prices ended steady in light range-bound trade on Friday, dealers said.
They said demand was poor and supplies limited.
In ready delivery, sugar S-30 was steady at 1,290/1,350 rupees per quintal and M-30 unchanged at 1,340/1,380 rupees per quintal.
"Arrivals were virtually nil from mills to the market due to the ongoing strike by transport operators," said a dealer.

Transport operations across India have been affected by a strike called by truck owners to protest an increase in insurance premium and the imposition of a service tax. Friday is the fourth day of the strike.
Delivery of sugar from the wholesale market to retail outlets was also poor due to the strike, dealers said.
Sugar mill delivery moved down 10/15 rupees to 1,200/1,220 rupees per quintal as millers were active sellers, dealers said.
"The transport strike has led to a stockpiling of stocks with mills," said a dealer. "This forced them to sell today."
